text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Switzerland's Federal Council wants to raise the value-added-tax rate by one percentage point, thereby earning an additional 1.5 billion Swiss francs by 1999 and 2.2 billion francs by the year 2005, in order to help finance increasing social security payments.

- The Swiss government has selected three non-Swiss, Elie Wiesel, Avraham Hirschon, and Josef Burg to help head the board of a newly-created Holocaust fund, along with four Swiss who were chosen two weeks ago.

- The Swiss Banking Association, the umbrella organisation of Swiss banks, announced it is ready to publicly release the names of bank account holders with unclaimed funds dating from the Holocaust period.
- Adecco reported a 29 percent increase in group sales for the first quarter of 1997.

- Kuoni Reisen Holding AG acquired a 50 percent stake in P & O Travel Ltd. in Hong Kong, retroactive as of January 1. - Swisscontrol posted a profit of 7.76 million Swiss francs for its first year after becoming financially independent in 1996.
- STG Coopers & Lybrand reported a 4.6 percent revenue increase to 321 million Swiss francs for 1996.

- Allgemeine Plakatgesellschaft posted a sales increase of five percent to 241 million Swiss francs for 1996. Profit however, fell by 10 percent down to 25 million Swiss francs. - Zurich Insurance Group's 1996 profit surged by 30.2 percent to 1.1 billion Swiss francs. Gross premiums rose by 20 percent to 32 billion francs, and the dividend will rise to 7.20 francs from six francs per share.

- More than 5,000 people marched through the inner city of Zurich yesterday on Labour Day under the motto "Work for Everyone". The demonstrations were quieter than last year due to better preparation by the police and some 100 people were arrested. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
